title: Bounded timeout of a clocked simulation
statement: Let $e:	ext{Bool}	o	ext{Γ}$ be an embedding, let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape machine over $	ext{Γ}$ with state set $S$, and let $\mathrm{stopAt}:S\to\text{Bool}$. Let $x$ be a finite input word and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$ whose state is $q$. Let $w$ be a Boolean word, let $ct:\mathbb Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\text{Γ})$ be a tape content function, and let $cp\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $ct(cp+p)$ equals the content at position $p$ of the tape storing the encoded word $w$ whenever $-1\le p\le |w|$. Write $N$ for the integer represented by the binary digits of $w$, and suppose that for every natural number $u\le N$, the configuration reached by running $M$ from $c$ for $u$ steps is not stopped by $\mathrm{stopAt}$. Then there are a natural number $T\le 5N+2|w|+2$ and a Boolean word $w'$ with $|w'|=|w|$ such that the clocked machine, started with body configuration $c$, clock head at $cp$, and clock state carrying $q$ in its forward counting phase, reaches after $T$ steps a timeout state carrying the state of $M$'s configuration after $N$ steps, with the body tapes, input-head position, and output equal to that configuration and the clock tape obtained by patching $ct$ with the encoding of $w'$ at base position $cp$. At every time $u<T$, the clocked machine is in neither its finish nor its timeout state. For every $u\le T$, there is a natural number $v\le N$ such that its body tapes, their head positions, input-head position, and output agree with those of $M$ after $v$ steps, and its clock-head position belongs to $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$.
